extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff; legal/regulatory professionals handling USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedures, and substantive standards governing USPTO disciplinary actions against registered practitioners, including jurisdiction, grounds for discipline, mitigation, sanctions (suspension/probation), publication, and procedures for lifting stays and reinstatement under 35 U.S.C. and 37 C.F.R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26; practitioners are subject to the disciplinary rules in 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that the Office may bring and adjudicate disciplinary complaints against registered agents/attorneys; needed to support issuance of Final Order and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline — violations of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations include engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct (10.23(a)), engaging in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude (10.23(b)(3)), and engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice before the Office (10.23(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions (here, Attempted Child Molestation in the Second Degree) can constitute violations of these provisions and support disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stipulated facts and settlement agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed settlement agreement resolving all disciplinary action based on stipulated facts may be submitted for approval and, if approved, the Final Order will set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can resolve the proceeding; Final Order memorializes admissions, legal findings, and agreed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction structure — suspension and stayed portion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent suspended from practice for sixty (60) months with the last twenty-four (24) months of the suspension stayed; respondent also placed on a sixty (60) month probationary period commencing nunc pro tunc to the suspension start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies duration and the concept of a partial stay (conditional non-enforcement of a portion of suspension) as a sanction structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility and restriction on practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may seek reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after serving the first thirty-six (36) months of suspension, unless the stay is lifted; nothing permits practice before reinstatement in accordance with § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets minimum served-time before application for reinstatement and reiterates that reinstatement is required before resuming practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary compliance requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation terms under § 11.58 govern behavior, reporting, and compliance; violation during probation can trigger further proceedings (see Order to Show Cause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall (A) issue an Order to Show Cause, (B) send it to respondent at the last address of record, and (C) grant respondent fifteen (15) days to respond; after consideration, the OED Director may present the matter to the USPTO Director to lift the stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure outlines notice, response period, transmission of order/response/evidence to USPTO Director, and request to lift the stayed portion of suspension if noncompliance is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, notice of public discipline and reasons shall be given to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies locations and means of dissemination (OED Reading Room, Official Gazette) and obligations to notify state agencies and courts per § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of public Notice of Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Suspension should identify the respondent (name, registration number), state the suspension and stayed portion, specify the provisions violated (e.g., 10.23(a), 10.23(b)(3), 10.23(b)(6)), summarize the underlying criminal conviction and facts, list sanctions and treatment requirements, and note mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a template-like description of what facts and conclusions are disclosed publicly about the disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating evidence (e.g., judge's factual statement about compliance with treatment and probation, demonstrated remorse, completion of programs, successful compliance with supervision) is considered in determining sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references the sentencing judge's monitoring and reports of compliance as mitigating; such evidence can support stays or lesser sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of compliance with court-ordered conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's compliance with court orders (e.g., DNA sample, HIV testing/counseling, sexual deviancy treatment, home detention, community supervision, victim penalty assessment, sex offender registration, polygraphs and urine analysis) bears on discipline and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented completion and compliance with court-ordered programs and monitoring are relevant to mitigation and to decisions about lifting restrictions over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of lifting the stay on suspension timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay of the last twenty-four months of suspension is lifted during probation and respondent seeks review of that decision, such review shall not postpone or hold in abeyance the additional and immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that appellate or review rights do not delay imposition of the additional suspension if stay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of this record in future disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered in future complaints or proceedings regarding the same or similar misconduct either as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Order may be used later to increase discipline or to counter respondent's claims; it remains part of disciplinary history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the settlement does not shift costs and that each party pays its own expenses unless otherwise ordered.
